name: Fat-loss to reveal neck
lead: Fat loss to reveal the neck refers to reducing body fat so that neck and submental contours look more defined. Wikipedia notes that a double chin can arise from excess fat around the neck in some overweight people, or from a bony deficiency in people of normal weight, and that the bony form usually needs surgical correction.[1]

Exercise physiology sources describe that fat is mobilized from the whole body rather than from the area being exercised, so spot reduction is not regarded as achievable by physiologists; where fat is lost first is strongly influenced by genetics.[2] No study found in this research has tested fat loss specifically for neck or jawline definition.
infobox: Submental fat, jaw and chin structure
Not supported by exercise physiology sources

paras: The Wikipedia article on double chin describes two causes: excess subcutaneous fat around the neck, and underdeveloped jaw bones that leave the chin blending into the neck. Fat-related cases may be treated by removing the fat pad, sometimes with a hyoid lift, while bone-related cases may need genioplasty or orthognathic surgery.[1]

The Wikipedia article on spot reduction states that physiologists and fitness bodies regard it as disproven and that fat loss follows overall diet and exercise, with genetics shaping where it is lost. It cites a 2011 study of 24 sedentary adults who did abdominal exercises for six weeks and showed no decrease in abdominal subcutaneous fat.[2] That study concerned the abdomen, not the neck.
No studies found on fat loss for neck or jawline appearance. Related research on abdominal exercise and regional fat is summarised above.[2]

card.summary: Getting leaner to show neck and jaw definition; fat distribution is genetic and bone structure matters too.
card.note: No studies on neck-specific fat loss; spot reduction is not supported by exercise science.

quick.overview:
The idea is that lowering body fat makes the neck and chin area look more defined. A double-chin look can come from fat or from jaw structure.

Exercise physiology sources say fat cannot be burned from one chosen area, and where it comes off first is largely genetic. No neck-specific studies were found.
quick.mechanism: Overall fat loss from diet and activity reduces subcutaneous fat including around the neck, in an order that varies between people. Bony causes of a soft profile are not changed by fat loss.
quick.risks: No specific risks are documented for this practice; general risks of aggressive dieting are outside the scope of the sources found.
